## Description {#description}

Students study how distributed training, communication, fault recovery, and serving work across many machines. The course ends with a design project that students defend in a written report.

## Learning outcomes {#outcomes}

By the end of the course, students can:

- Choose a parallelism strategy for a training workload and justify it with measurements.
- Explain how a training job recovers its progress after failures.
- Size a serving system for a stated demand, cost, and energy budget.
- Defend a fleet design in a written report.

## Assessment {#assessment}

A suggested split; each offering sets its own.

| Component | Weight |
|:---|:---|
| Lab Decision Logs (Labs 01–16) | 40% |
| Design challenges (one per part) | 30% |
| Capstone: a fleet design with evidence, a report, and a presentation | 30% |

## Suggested papers {#papers}

Optional readings that pair with the chapters, for a seminar or a graduate section.

| Week | Topic | Paper |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | Scale Imperative | Kaplan et al., "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" (2020) |
| 5 | Collective Comms | Narayanan et al., "Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters" (2021) |
| 6 | Distributed Training | Shoeybi et al., "Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models" (2020) |
| 7 | Fault Tolerance | Jeon et al., "Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters" (ATC 2019) |
| 10 | Inference at Scale | Kwon et al., "Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention" (SOSP 2023) |
| 12 | Ops at Scale | Zhao et al., "Characterizing GPU Cluster Failures at Scale" (ATC 2024) |
| 15 | Sustainability | Patterson et al., "Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training" (2021) |

## Adapting this syllabus {#adapting}

- Each offering sets its own dates, deadlines, and policies on late work, collaboration, and AI tools.
- **Two semesters:** this course follows [Introduction to Machine Learning Systems](foundations-syllabus.qmd).
